title: Reno picks 35% more units per hour than Allentown, and most of the gap comes from slotting and pick paths, not people
subtitle: A benchmark of pick productivity across our four fulfilment centres, with the gap broken down by cause and a plan for spreading Reno's practices to the other sites.
summary: From January to April, pick productivity ranged from 62 units per labour hour at Reno to 46 at Allentown, against a network average of 53. A shift-level model attributes 83% of the Reno–Allentown gap to slotting, pick-path travel and batch size, and only 11% to associate tenure. Moving Allentown and Columbus halfway to Reno's practices would save about 21,800 pick hours (≈$0.53M) a year.
key_findings: Jan–Apr 2026 pick rate: Reno 62 UPH, Dallas 55, Columbus 51, Allentown 46; network 53.
Of the 16 UPH Reno–Allentown gap, slotting explains 5.8, pick-path travel 4.3, batch size 3.2 and tenure only 1.8.
UPH rises from 41 at 1–4 orders per batch to 58 at 9–12 and then levels off; Allentown averages 6.4 orders per batch against Reno's 11.2.
New pickers start at ~29 UPH and reach the network average around week 12.
Closing half the gap at Allentown and Columbus would save ~21,800 pick hours (≈$0.53M) a year.
